passages.context: Defines Egyptian artificial preservation by dehydration and describes a reconstructed classic process involving organ removal, natron desiccation over forty days, further preparation, oils or incense, and final linen wrapping. The methodological caution on p. 4 prevents treating Egyptian practice as one uniform recipe.
passages.notes: Used only as a contrast with the much less specific Johannine description; it supplies no evidence about Jewish burial practice.
